description: Four low-frequency oscillators of fixed shape, two ADSR envelopes each with its own VCA, and a noise source, all on one panel

params.text: Sets the rate of the sawtooth oscillator, 0.125Hz to 256Hz
Sets the rate of the triangle oscillator, 0.125Hz to 256Hz
Sets the rate of the square oscillator, 0.125Hz to 256Hz
Sets the rate of the sine oscillator, 0.125Hz to 256Hz
Sets the part of each cycle the square oscillator spends high, 0 to 100 per cent
Holds all four oscillators at the start of their cycle for as long as it is pressed, and lets them run from there when it is released
Sets the attack of the first envelope, the time it takes to climb to 10V, 0 to 4 seconds
Sets the decay of the first envelope, the time it takes to fall from 10V to the sustain level, 0 to 4 seconds
Sets the level the first envelope holds while its gate stays high, 0 to 100 per cent of 10V
Sets the release of the first envelope, the time it takes to fall back to 0V after its gate drops, 0 to 4 seconds
Sets the attack of the second envelope, the time it takes to climb to 10V, 0 to 4 seconds
Sets the decay of the second envelope, the time it takes to fall from 10V to the sustain level, 0 to 4 seconds
Sets the level the second envelope holds while its gate stays high, 0 to 100 per cent of 10V
Sets the release of the second envelope, the time it takes to fall back to 0V after its gate drops, 0 to 4 seconds

inputs.text: Sets all four oscillators back to the start of their cycle on each rising edge above 1V
Opens the first envelope on each channel rising above 0.5V and releases it when that channel falls back; the number of channels patched here sets how many voices the envelope runs
The signal the first envelope's VCA multiplies, channel by channel: it passes through unchanged at 10V of envelope and is silenced at 0V
Opens the second envelope on each channel rising above 0.5V and releases it when that channel falls back; the number of channels patched here sets how many voices the envelope runs
The signal the second envelope's VCA multiplies, channel by channel: it passes through unchanged at 10V of envelope and is silenced at 0V

outputs.text: The sawtooth, rising 0V to 10V over each cycle, or -5V to 5V with LFO 1 checked on the menu
The sawtooth turned over, falling 10V to 0V over each cycle, or the negative of the sawtooth with LFO 1 checked on the menu
The triangle, 0V to 10V and back over each cycle, or -5V to 5V with LFO 2 checked on the menu
The triangle turned over, so that it falls where the triangle rises, over the same range
The square, 0V while the cycle is low and 10V while it is high, or -5V and 5V with LFO 3 checked on the menu
The square turned over, high where the square is low, over the same range
The sine, 0V to 10V over each cycle, or -5V to 5V with LFO 4 checked on the menu
The sine turned over, falling where the sine rises, over the same range
White noise drawn fresh every sample, -5V to 5V, or 0V to 10V with Noise unchecked on the menu; the menu also sets how many channels it carries
The first envelope, 0V to 10V, with one channel for each channel of its gate jack
The first envelope's VCA input multiplied by the envelope, channel by channel
The second envelope, 0V to 10V, with one channel for each channel of its gate jack
The second envelope's VCA input multiplied by the envelope, channel by channel

notes: an envelope does nothing at all until a cable is patched to its gate jack: with that jack empty its two outputs are left untouched at whatever they last carried
the four oscillators have fixed shapes and cannot be changed: the first is a sawtooth, the second a triangle, the third a square and the fourth a sine
the four oscillators share one reset, so the button and the reset jack line all of them up at once whatever their rates
menu: Noise channels — sets how many channels the noise output carries, 1 to 16, each drawn separately
Polarity (check = bipolar) — a heading over the five items below it, one for each oscillator and one for the noise
LFO 1 — checked, the sawtooth and its inverted twin run -5V to 5V instead of 0V to 10V
LFO 2 — checked, the triangle and its inverted twin run -5V to 5V instead of 0V to 10V
LFO 3 — checked, the square and its inverted twin run -5V to 5V instead of 0V to 10V
LFO 4 — checked, the sine and its inverted twin run -5V to 5V instead of 0V to 10V
Noise — checked, the noise output runs -5V to 5V; unchecked it runs 0V to 10V. It comes up checked

inputs.0:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
high above 0.5V · stepped · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the envelope does not run; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.3:
high above 0.5V · stepped · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the envelope does not run; a negative voltage does nothing here.
